ledger.note: 1499: Louis XII enters Milan (6 October). Ludovico was captured at Novara in April 1500. Cliopatria's Duchy of Milan row has no shape 1502-1525 and the France shape adds the Lombard cells in 1502.

region.text: 'On 6 October 1499, Louis made a triumphant entry into Milan'

ledger.note: 1501: Naples is taken (Capua surrenders on 24 July). Treaty of Granada of 11 November 1500 had agreed 'to divide the kingdom between the two' powers.

region.text: Capua 'surrendered on 24 July [1501]'

ledger.note: 1503: the French are expelled from Naples after Garigliano (29 December). The page's 'once again' refers to 1502-1503; year of Garigliano is my reading; Cliopatria keeps Naples to 1506.

region.text: 'expelled from Naples once again after defeats at ... Garigliano on 29 December'

ledger.note: 1512: the Swiss retake Milan. League of Cambrai section; Ravenna was a French victory (11 April 1512). Cliopatria has no Milan shape 1502-1525.

region.text: 'the Swiss recaptured Milan and restored Ludovico's son'

ledger.note: 1515: Francis I wins at Marignano and retakes Milan. Noyon, 13 August 1516, 'acknowledged Francis as duke of Milan'; Brussels, December 1516, confirmed it.

region.text: 'routed the Swiss at Marignano on 13-14 September 1515'; 'victory allowed Francis to retake Milan'

ledger.note: November 1521: an Imperial-Papal army under Prospero Colonna and the Marquis of Pescara captures Milan and restores Francesco II Sforza; the French attempt to retake it ends at Bicocca on 27 April 1522 (Italian Wars page). The page does not say the French held Milan again before Pavia (24 February 1525), where it records only 'a devastating defeat'; the earlier dating of this loss to February 1525 is replaced.

region.text: 'captured Milan and restored Francesco II Sforza as duke'

ledger.note: August 1523: Francis I sequesters the Bourbon lands in dispute after Suzanne's death; Charles III, who signed a treaty with the Emperor in July 1523, breaks with the crown. The page names no region; Auvergne and Bourbonnais are the two the Crown lands page lists for the 1531 confiscation. house-of-bourbon /ledger/7 records the same August 1523 as a loss, the confiscation of 1531 follows here as the gain.

region.text: 'In August 1523, all the disputed lands were sequestered from Bourbon'

ledger.note: 1531: the sequestered Bourbon lands are confiscated and annexed (next event).

region.text: 'possessions of the disgraced Charles III, Duke of Bourbon, are confiscated: Bourbonnais, Auvergne'

ledger.note: 1531: the possessions of the disgraced Charles III, Duke of Bourbon, are confiscated, after the sequestration of August 1523 (occupation above). Crown lands page: 'the appanage of the House of Bourbon however remains alienated'; the Charles III page adds that Dombes was 'returned to the Bourbon-Montpensier family in 1560' and that the legal dispute lasted until Charles IX. The region is my reading; Cliopatria adds the Auvergne-Limousin-Bourbonnais block in 1540. house-of-bourbon /ledger/7 loses the lands in August 1523; the Bourbon owner should record that as an occupation by this state and the 1531 loss.

region.text: 'possessions of the disgraced Charles III, Duke of Bourbon are confiscated'

ledger.note: 1532: Brittany is united with France (the Kingdom of France page gives 1453 and 1547 for Brittany).

region.text: 'union of the Duchy of Brittany with France'

ledger.note: 1532: Brittany joins the kingdom for good. Crown lands page, entry 1532; 1547 is 'the final step in the personal union'.

region.text: 'union of the Duchy of Brittany with France'

ledger.note: 1536: a French army occupies Turin and Piedmont. The Truce of Nice (18 June 1538) 'left France in possession of most of Savoy, Piedmont and Artois'; Crepy (14 September 1544) 'essentially restored the position to that prevailing in 1542'. Cliopatria's County of Savoy row ends in 1539 and the France shape adds the land in 1540.

region.text: 'a French army under Philippe de Chabot occupied Turin'; Pinerolo, Chieri and Carmagnola

ledger.note: 1552: Henry II takes the Three Bishoprics (Treaty of Chambord, January 1552). France 'retained Calais and the Three Bishoprics' at Cateau-Cambresis. Cliopatria adds 31 Lorraine cells in 1552.

region.text: 'the Three Bishoprics of Toul, Verdun, and Metz'

ledger.note: 1553: a Franco-Ottoman force takes Corsica from Genoa.

region.text: 'a Franco-Ottoman force captured the Genoese island of Corsica'

ledger.note: 1558: the French retake Calais (January). Crown lands page: 'French reconquest and incorporation of Calais into the Crown lands' (1558).

region.text: 'in January 1558 the French took Calais'

ledger.note: 1559: Cateau-Cambresis (3 April) returns Corsica to Genoa.

region.text: 'Corsica was returned to Genoa'

ledger.note: 1559: Cateau-Cambresis restores Savoy and Piedmont. The page names neither; the land is my reading; Cliopatria keeps them in the France shape to 1563 and its House of Savoy row begins in 1564.

region.text: 'other provisions essentially returned the position to that prevailing in 1551'

ledger.note: 1564: the Bourbon block leaves the shape. No page opened dates this (confidence 1): the date and land rest on the Cliopatria shapes (Cliopatria's House of Bourbon row is 74,000 km2 from 1556). The Crown lands page keeps the Bourbon appanage 'alienated' after 1531 and lists the Albret, Armagnac, Foix and Bigorre lands among Henry IV's personal domain merged in 1589; house-of-bourbon has no matching 1564 gain (its 1555 gain is the Albret inheritance), so the Bourbon owner should reconcile it.

region.text: the Auvergne-Limousin-Guyenne-Bourbonnais block that leaves the shape in 1564

ledger.note: 1589: Henry IV, first Bourbon, succeeds the last Valois. 2 August 1589 ('Valois line ends with him'); same state, same colour (rule 2).

1589: Henry III of Navarre becomes Henry IV of France and his lands join the crown. Crown lands page, entry 1589; the Henry IV page: 'nominally became king' and the League prevented 'universal recognition'. Cliopatria's House of Bourbon row ends in 1594 and the shape adds 312 cells in 1595; the 1607 edict of union is not on the page.

region.text: the lands of the House of Bourbon (Auvergne, Limousin, Guyenne, Gascony, Languedoc, Bourbonnais, Lyonnais) joined to the crown with Henry IV

ledger.note: 1589: Navarre and Bearn stay a separate kingdom under the same king. Crown lands page, entry 1589; Navarre page: 'In 1589, Henry became the sole rightful claimant to the crown of France'.

region.text: 'Navarre remained independent in personal union'

ledger.note: 1601: France gives up Saluzzo in the Treaty of Lyon territorial exchanges. The page says Henry first sought to keep Saluzzo for Bresse and that the treaty 'arranged territorial exchanges'; Cliopatria drops Piedmont cells already in 1588.

region.text: Saluzzo, the disputed territory 'arranged' by the Treaty of Lyon

ledger.note: 1601: the Treaty of Lyon gives France Bresse, Bugey and Gex. Henry IV page (January 1601); Ain is my reading.

region.text: 'In January 1601, Henry accepted another offer of papal arbitration and gained not only Bresse, but Bugey and Gex'

ledger.note: 1620: Lower Navarre and Bearn are merged into France. 'Between 1620 and 1624, Lower Navarre and Bearn were incorporated into France proper'; Crown lands page: 1620.

region.text: 'in 1620 it was merged into the Kingdom of France'

ledger.note: 1620: Lower Navarre and Bearn become part of the kingdom.

region.text: Lower Navarre and Bearn

ledger.note: 1636: Cliopatria draws Lorraine inside the France shape from 1636. The page is silent on this; the date and land rest on the Cliopatria shapes (confidence 1). The page only says the Westphalia peace excluded 'French-occupied Lorraine' (1648).

region.text: 'French-occupied Lorraine'

ledger.note: 1636: the Spanish reach Corbie in the war France declared in May 1635. Franco-Spanish War page. The same zone carries the French hold on Artois from 1640 (the Cliopatria 1640 shape adds Artois cells); it is closed by the 1659 gain.

region.text: 'A Spanish incursion into northern France reached as far as Corbie in August'

ledger.note: 1640: Picardy and Alsace cells join the shape. The page is silent on this; the date and land rest on the Cliopatria shapes (confidence 1). The Artois cells are no longer a gain here: Artois is the contest zone of the war from August 1636 and is gained once, in 1659 (Treaty of the Pyrenees).

region.text: the cells (Picardy, Alsace) that Cliopatria adds in 1640 other than Artois

ledger.counterpart: Picardy and Alsace (holder not named by the pages opened)

ledger.note: 1641: Catalonia accepts Louis XIII. Franco-Spanish War page; Cliopatria's Catalonia row is 1640-1641 only.

region.text: 'the Catalan Courts recognised Louis XIII as Count of Barcelona and ruler of the Principality of Catalonia'

ledger.note: 1642: France seizes Roussillon; the Treaty of the Pyrenees makes it French in 1659 (occupation_end and gain below). The Kingdom of France page: 'formalised France's seizure (1642) of ... Roussillon'.

region.text: 'France's seizure (1642) of ... Roussillon'

ledger.note: 1648: the Peace of Westphalia gives France strategic places in Alsace. Kingdom of France page: 'Alsace: Peace of Westphalia (1648)'; the page says Cliopatria's Lorraine occupation was excluded from the peace.

region.text: 'France gained strategic locations in Alsace and Lorraine' (Treaty of Münster, October 1648)

ledger.note: 1648: Breisach is given to France at Westphalia ('In the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, Breisach was de jure given to France'); returned to the Empire at Ryswick in 1697, recaptured on 7 September 1703, returned at Rastatt on 7 March 1714.

region.text: 'Breisach was de jure given to France'

ledger.note: 1652: Spain recaptures Barcelona and Catalonia leaves French protection. Year from the page; the region is my reading.

region.text: 'During 1652, Spain recaptured both Dunkirk and Barcelona'

ledger.note: 1659: the occupation of Lorraine ends. The page is silent on this; the date and land rest on the Cliopatria shapes (confidence 1). The page does not describe Lorraine's return; Cliopatria's Duchy of Lorraine row has shapes in 1648-1672 beside the France shape.

region.text: French-occupied Lorraine

ledger.note: 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees ends the war (5 November in the page body, 7 November in the infobox).

region.text: northern France and the Spanish Netherlands frontier

ledger.note: November 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees (signed 5 November 1659) turns the seizure of Roussillon into a cession. 'Acquisition of Roussillon established the Franco-Spanish border along the Pyrenees.'

region.text: 'France gained Artois and Hainaut ... as well as Roussillon'

ledger.note: 1659: France gains Artois, Hainaut and Roussillon by the Treaty of the Pyrenees. Kingdom of France page: 'County of Artois (1659)', Roussillon and Perpignan.

region.text: 'France gained Artois and Hainaut along its border with the Spanish Netherlands, as well as Roussillon'

ledger.note: 1663: French troops invade the papal Comtat Venaissin (infobox 'French occupation: 1663, 1668, 1768-1774'; 'during disputes between the Crown and the Church').

region.text: 'invaded by French troops in 1663, 1668 and 1768-1774 during disputes between the Crown and the Church'

ledger.note: 1663: the occupation is bridged as lasting that year; the page gives no end for it. The Comtat stayed papal (mirror: comtat-venaissin /ledger/3-4).

region.text: 'invaded by French troops in 1663, 1668 and 1768-1774 during disputes between the Crown and the Church'

ledger.note: 24 May 1667: Louis XIV crosses into the Spanish Netherlands in the War of Devolution; Charleroi falls first (2 June), Tournai, Courtrai and Oudenaarde by the end of July, Lille on 28 August.

region.text: 'The French crossed the border on 24 May'; Charleroi, Tournai, Kortrijk, Oudenaarde and Lille taken in 1667

ledger.note: 1668: French troops invade the Comtat Venaissin again (same infobox line).

region.text: 'invaded by French troops in 1663, 1668 and 1768-1774 during disputes between the Crown and the Church'

ledger.note: 1668: bridged as lasting that year; the page gives no end for it (mirror: comtat-venaissin /ledger/5-6).

region.text: 'invaded by French troops in 1663, 1668 and 1768-1774 during disputes between the Crown and the Church'

ledger.note: February 1668: Conde's forces enter Franche-Comte on 4 February; Besancon and Salins surrender on 7 February, Dole on 14 February, Gray on the 19th (War of Devolution page). The Franco-Dutch War page speaks of 'Franche-Comte, 1667-1668'; the War of Devolution page dates the entry to February 1668.

region.text: 'Conde's forces entered the province on 4 February' 1668

ledger.note: 2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle returns Franche-Comte to Spain ('France withdrew from Franche-Comte and most of the Spanish Netherlands').

region.text: 'France withdrew from Franche-Comte' (Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, 2 May 1668)

ledger.note: 2 May 1668: the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the War of Devolution.

region.text: 'It was signed on 2 May 1668 in Aachen'

ledger.note: 2 May 1668: France keeps nine Flemish towns by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle: 'he kept Armentieres, Bergues, Charleroi, Courtrai, Douai, Furnes, Lille, Oudenarde, and Tournai' (the War of Devolution page also lists Binche and Ath among the retained towns). Cliopatria's 1670 shape carries only some of these cells (Lille, Tournai, Veurne, Armentieres).

region.text: 'he kept Armentieres, Bergues, Charleroi, Courtrai, Douai, Furnes, Lille, Oudenarde, and Tournai' (Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle page)

ledger.note: 1670: Louis XIV overruns the Duchy of Lorraine (mid-1670). Cliopatria adds the Lorraine cells in 1673.

region.text: 'when over-running the Duchy of Lorraine in mid 1670'

ledger.note: June 1672: the French overrun Utrecht (14 June, the council hands over the keys of the gates), Naarden (19 June) and Nijmegen in Gelderland (9 July). The page says France 'failed to conquer the Dutch Republic' and 'did not continue his advance to the west'; Overijssel surrendered 'to the bishop of Munster', not to France, so the occupation covers Utrecht and Gelderland, not the whole country.

region.text: 'the council of Utrecht delivered the keys of the gates'; 'the French took the fortress of Naarden'; 'Nijmegen had been taken on 9 July'

ledger.note: 1674: Louis evacuates Utrecht and Gelderland after the Dutch take Bonn in late 1673; 'the next year only Grave and Maastricht remained in French hands' (Grave was recaptured in October 1674, Maastricht stayed; the page does not say when it was returned).

region.text: 'Louis was forced to evacuate French troops from the Dutch Republic'

ledger.note: 1674: France overruns Franche-Comte in six weeks.

region.text: 'In the spring of 1674, the French invaded ... They overran the entire province in less than six weeks'

ledger.note: November 1677: the French capture Freiburg ('the French commander succeeded in capturing Freiburg in November 1677'); the Nijmegen infobox lists 'Lorraine, Freiburg, and Kehl' among the French gains. Returned to the Empire at Ryswick (1697), recaptured in November 1713 and returned at Rastatt in March 1714.

region.text: 'capturing Freiburg in November 1677'

ledger.note: 1678: France takes Kehl, across the Rhine from Strasbourg ('In 1678, the city was taken over by France'; Vauban fortifies it in 1683). Ryswick returns it to the Empire in 1697 (the page has it ceded to Baden in 1698), the French recapture it in 1703 and Rastatt returns it in 1714.

region.text: 'In 1678, the city was taken over by France'

ledger.note: March 1678: Louis captures Ghent ('captured Ypres and Ghent in early March', before the Dutch treaty of 10 August 1678; the sentence gives no year, which the date of the treaty supplies).

region.text: 'captured Ypres and Ghent in early March'

ledger.note: 1678: Spain cedes Franche-Comte at Nijmegen. War dates 6 April 1672 to 17 September 1678.

region.text: 'receiving the entire Franche-Comte'

ledger.note: 1678: France gains Franche-Comte, Ypres, Maubeuge, Cateau-Cambresis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel at Nijmegen. The Kingdom of France page also lists 'French Hainaut (1679)' and the Free County of Burgundy at 1679.

region.text: 'the entire Franche-Comte and the towns of Ypres, Maubeuge, Cateau-Cambresis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel'

ledger.note: September 1678: France gives Charleroi back to Spain at Nijmegen (gained in 1668 at Aix-la-Chapelle; the Nijmegen infobox: 'Spain regains Ath and Charleroi'). Ghent's return and the other towns are the events that follow.

region.text: 'France returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns in the Spanish Netherlands'

ledger.note: September 1678: France returns Ghent to Spain at Nijmegen ('France returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns in the Spanish Netherlands').

region.text: 'France returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns'

ledger.note: September 1678: France gives back 'other towns in the Spanish Netherlands' at Nijmegen. The page does not name them; Courtrai and Oudenarde, which the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle page lists among the towns France kept in 1668, are in Cliopatria's 1677 shape and absent from its 1683 shape.

region.text: Courtrai and Oudenarde, 'other towns' returned at Nijmegen (my reading)

ledger.note: 1681: France seizes Strasbourg (30 September). The same page gives both 'seized in 1681' and 'On 30 September 1685, French troops also seized Strasbourg and its outpost, Kehl'; the 1681 reading is mine.

region.text: 'Strasbourg (seized in 1681)'

ledger.note: 1682: the court settles at Versailles. Infobox: 'Versailles (unofficially, 1682-1789)'; Paris stays the formal capital.
1683: the War of the Reunions opens in Flanders (Dixmude, December; the page gives no year for it, 1683 is my reading).

region.text: 'followed by Dixmude in December and Luxembourg in June 1684'

ledger.note: 1684: France takes Luxembourg (June). 'Spain regained Luxembourg and other territories from France' at Ryswick.

region.text: 'Luxembourg in June 1684'

ledger.note: 1684: the Truce of Ratisbon (15 August) guarantees the new borders for twenty years.

region.text: the reunited lands

ledger.note: 1688: France invades the Palatinate and the Rhine. The page records scorched earth in the Palatinate, Baden and Wurttemberg (Heidelberg torched on 2 March 1689).

region.text: 'besieged the Elector of Trier's fortress of Philippsburg on 27 September 1688'; 'Mannheim ... capitulated on 11 November'

ledger.note: 1690: Catinat wins at Staffarda and France holds Savoy and Nice. The occupation of Savoy and Nice is my reading of the shape that adds 126 cells in 1691.

region.text: 'Nicolas Catinat ... soundly defeated Victor Amadeus at the Battle of Staffarda on 18 August'

ledger.note: 1694: France takes Palamos and Girona. Barcelona fell on 10 August 1697 ('besieged and captured Barcelona').

region.text: 'the French proceeded to take Palamos on 10 June, Gerona on 29 June, and Hostalric'

ledger.note: 1696: the Treaty of Turin ends the Savoy front; Pinerolo is handed back with its fortifications demolished.

region.text: 'The terms were formalised as the Treaty of Turin on 29 August 1696'

ledger.note: 1697: Ryswick (20 September) returns the Catalan places.

region.text: 'Spain regained Luxembourg and other territories from France'

ledger.note: 1697: Ryswick returns Lorraine to Duke Leopold. Cliopatria keeps it in the France shape; the dossier removes it from 1698.

region.text: 'France returns ... Lorraine to Duke Leopold'

ledger.note: 1697: the Peace of Ryswick ends the Nine Years' War (20 September); 'French control over the entirety of Alsace was officially recognized'.

region.text: reunion gains on the right bank of the Rhine 'relinquished and restored to their rulers'

ledger.note: 1697: France returns Luxembourg and Kortrijk to Spain.

region.text: 'France returns Luxembourg and Kortrijk to Spain'

ledger.note: 1697: France returns Freiburg, Breisach and Kehl to the Empire. Kehl is placed by coordinates (no gazetteer entry).

region.text: 'Freiburg, Breisach, and Kehl to the Holy Roman Empire'

ledger.note: 1702: Imperial forces take Landau. 'Imperial forces under Louis William, Margrave of Baden-Baden remained on the defensive, although they took Landau in 1702.' The pages opened do not say when France acquired Landau, so this ledger has no earlier gain for it.

region.text: 'they took Landau in 1702'

ledger.note: 1703: French troops occupy Savoy after Victor Amadeus II changes sides (War of the Spanish Succession page: 'In October 1703, Victor Amadeus declared war on France'). The Duchy of Savoy infobox gives the occupation as 1703-13; the page does not give the month the French entered.

region.text: 'Occupied by France: 1536-59, 1630, 1690-96, 1703-13' (Duchy of Savoy infobox)

ledger.note: 1703: the French overrun the Piedmontese lands of Savoy. 'By May 1706, the French held most of Savoy except Turin' (the page's Savoy is the Savoyard state; the page does not date the Piedmont campaigns beyond 1703-1706).

region.text: 'by May 1706, the French held most of Savoy except Turin'

ledger.note: 1703: French forces retake Landau and capture Kehl and Breisach (Breisach on 7 September 1703, Breisach page). 'During the 1703 campaign French forces retook Landau, won victories at Friedlingen, Hochstadt and Speyerbach, then captured Kehl and Breisach.'

region.text: Breisach, Kehl and Landau, recaptured in 1703

ledger.note: September 1706: Turin is relieved and the French lose Piedmont. 'Prince Eugene broke the siege of Turin in September'; 'by the end of 1707, fighting in Italy ceased, apart from minor attempts by Victor Amadeus to recover Nice and Savoy', so only Nice and Savoy stayed French. The page does not say the French left Savoy in 1706: Savoy and Nice stay occupied (events below).

region.text: 'Prince Eugene broke the siege of Turin in September'

ledger.note: 1707: the French occupy the County of Nice. 'the county was subjected to French occupation twice (1691-1697 and 1707-1713)'.

region.text: 'French occupation twice (1691-1697 and 1707-1713)'

ledger.note: 22 October 1708: Boufflers surrenders Lille to the Allies (the citadel follows on 9 December). The Lille page has the Dutch occupy the city 'from 1708 to 1713'; the War of the Spanish Succession page: 'the Allies managed to capture Lille, the strongest fortress of the French fortress belts'.

region.text: 'on 22 October Boufflers surrendered the city to the Allies'

ledger.note: 1713: Lille returns to France when the Dutch occupation ends. 'For five years, from 1708 to 1713, the Dutch continued to occupy the city'; the page has it 'definitively attached to the France of Louis XIV following the War of Spanish Succession' without a date. The Peace of Utrecht (11 April 1713) is the settlement, but no page opened names Lille in it.

region.text: 'from 1708 to 1713, the Dutch continued to occupy the city'

ledger.note: 1713: the French occupation of Savoy ends with the war (infobox 1703-13). The Treaty of Utrecht page has the France-Savoy truce on 14 March 1713 and the peace on 11 April 1713; neither page says in so many words that Savoy was handed back.

region.text: 'Occupied by France: 1536-59, 1630, 1690-96, 1703-13' (Duchy of Savoy infobox)

ledger.note: 1713: the French occupation of the County of Nice ends (1707-1713, County of Nice page).

region.text: 'French occupation twice (1691-1697 and 1707-1713)'

region.text: 'France cedes Ypres, Tournai, Menen, Veurne, Fort Knokke, and Warneton to Austria'

region.text: 'the Principality of Orange'

ledger.note: 1713: France gains the Ubaye Valley (Utrecht). The page names no cedent; Savoy is my reading.

region.text: 'returned Breisach, Kehl, and Freiburg'

wars.outcome: Louis, called in by rebellious English barons, was defeated by English loyalists; naval defeat at Sandwich on 24 August 1217 and the Treaty of Lambeth (amnesty for the rebels) ended it. No French territory in England was kept.
wars.note: Cliopatria's 1216-1219 France shape includes south-eastern England (90 cells); the dossier removes it and records a contest zone 1216-1217.

wars.name: Conquest of Poitou (Louis VIII, 1224)

zones.text: 'seizing Poitou (in 1224), La Rochelle (August 1224)'; 'By the end of summer 1224, Louis had conquered Limousin, Perigord, and Quercy'

wars.outcome: French conquest of Poitou, La Rochelle, Limousin, Perigord and Quercy from the English crown; the English kept only the south-west (Gascony).
wars.note: The Crown lands page dates the confiscation of Poitou, Saintonge, Angouleme, Perigord and part of the Bordelais to 1223; the Louis VIII page gives 1224. The dossier follows the campaign page.

wars.name: Albigensian Crusade (royal campaign of 1226)

zones.text: 'Louis's campaign in 1226 captured numerous cities in Languedoc'; 1229 'the sénéchaussées of Nîmes' ceded to the king

wars.outcome: Louis VIII took numerous Languedoc cities in 1226 (Avignon surrendered on 9 September) and left the crown holding much of Languedoc; the Treaty of Paris of 1229 ceded the sénéchaussées of Nîmes to the king (the Crown lands page names no others).
wars.note: Only the royal phase is recorded; the Crusade itself began earlier and its earlier course was not opened (page budget). The Crown lands page is the source of the 1229 treaty.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War

zones.text: Caen 1417, Rouen 19 January 1419, French reconquest 1449-1450 (Formigny)
Gascony and Bordeaux, confiscated 1337, English again 1360-1369 and 1452, French 19 October 1453
Calais, captured by Edward III in 1347 and held until 1558

wars.outcome: Intermittent war 24 May 1337 to 19 October 1453: Calais lost 1347, Bretigny (8 May 1360) cedes increased lands in Aquitaine, Charles V reconquers 1369-1380, Henry V takes Normandy 1417-1419 and Troyes (1420) makes him heir, Joan of Arc and Charles VII turn the war from 1429, Arras (Sept 1435) returns Paris, Normandy is retaken 1449-1450 and Bordeaux falls on 19 October 1453; the English keep only Calais.
wars.note: The page's three phases are the Edwardian War (1337-1360), the Caroline War (1369-1389) and the Lancastrian War (1415-1453). The Treaty of Picquigny (1475) formally ended the war per the page.

wars.name: Burgundian Wars

zones.text: 'seize numerous Burgundian territories, including Burgundy itself and Picardy'

wars.outcome: Charles the Bold was killed at Nancy on 5 January 1477; Louis XI seized Burgundy and Picardy and the Treaty of Arras of 1482 left the Burgundian lands reverting to the crown of France.
wars.note: The page ties the end of the Burgundian Wars to Nancy (5 Jan 1477) but gives no start year; 'from' is the year of the French seizure, the first year the page supports.

wars.name: Italian Wars

zones.text: Naples, entered 1495, taken 1501, lost after Garigliano (29 December 1503)
Milan: entered 6 October 1499, lost 1512, retaken after Marignano (13-14 September 1515), lost in November 1521 (no French return before Pavia, 24 February 1525)
Turin occupied April 1536; Truce of Nice 18 June 1538; restored by Cateau-Cambresis
the Three Bishoprics of Toul, Verdun and Metz, 1552
captured 1553 by a Franco-Ottoman force; returned to Genoa 1559

wars.outcome: France gains Milan and Naples briefly and loses both; at Cateau-Cambresis (3 April 1559) France 'retained Calais and the Three Bishoprics' and returned Corsica; the other provisions 'essentially returned the position to that prevailing in 1551'.

wars.name: French Wars of Religion (Henry IV's war for the throne)
wars.outcome: Henry of Navarre became king on the death of Henry III but the League 'was strong enough to prevent a universal recognition'; the Edict of Nantes and the Peace of Vervins (both 1598) ended the wars. The page gives no territorial change.
wars.note: Only Henry IV's phase was read; the earlier phase from 1562 was not opened (page budget). Territory merges through the 1589 accession (Bourbon lands) and the 1601 Treaty of Lyon, both in the ledger.

wars.name: Reapers' War (Catalan Revolt)

zones.text: 'In 1641, the Catalan Courts recognised Louis XIII as Count of Barcelona and ruler of the Principality of Catalonia'

wars.outcome: Catalonia revolted in 1640 and accepted Louis XIII in 1641; 'During 1652, Spain recaptured both Dunkirk and Barcelona'.
wars.note: Part of the Franco-Spanish War; Roussillon stayed French (seized 1642, ceded 1659).

wars.name: Franco-Spanish War (1635-1659)

zones.text: Spanish incursion 'as far as Corbie' (August 1636); Artois ceded 1659
Hainaut ceded 1659
Roussillon, seized 1642, ceded 1659
'strategic locations in Alsace and Lorraine' by the Treaty of Munster, October 1648

wars.outcome: France declared war in May 1635. Westphalia (Oct 1648) gave France strategic locations in Alsace and Lorraine; the Treaty of the Pyrenees (5 or 7 November 1659 - the page's body and infobox disagree) gave France Artois, Hainaut and Roussillon.

wars.name: War of Devolution

zones.text: Charleroi, Tournai, Courtrai, Oudenaarde and Lille taken in 1667 ('The French crossed the border on 24 May'); nine towns kept at Aix-la-Chapelle
entered 4 February 1668, Dole surrendered 14 February; returned by the treaty

wars.outcome: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, 2 May 1668: France withdrew from Franche-Comte and most of the Spanish Netherlands but kept Armentieres, Bergues, Charleroi, Courtrai, Douai, Furnes, Lille, Oudenaarde and Tournai (the War of Devolution page also lists Binche and Ath).
wars.note: The war ran from May 1667 to May 1668; the Triple Alliance of England and the Dutch Republic was signed on 23 January 1668 and Sweden joined on 5 May. The Franco-Dutch War page says France 'relinquished many of his gains'.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War

zones.text: Utrecht (keys of the gates, 14 June 1672), Naarden (19 June) and Nijmegen (9 July); 'did not continue his advance to the west'; evacuated after November 1673
overrun in the spring of 1674 'in less than six weeks'; ceded by Spain at Nijmegen
Ypres, Maubeuge, Cateau-Cambresis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel at Nijmegen

wars.outcome: Treaties of Nijmegen (August-September 1678): France gained Franche-Comte and the towns of Ypres, Maubeuge, Cateau-Cambresis, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer and Cassel and returned Charleroi, Ghent and other towns; the Dutch 'ended the war without losing an inch of their own territory'.
wars.note: Infobox war dates 6 April 1672 to 17 September 1678.

wars.name: War of the Reunions

zones.text: Dixmude (December) and Luxembourg (June 1684)

wars.outcome: France took Luxembourg in June 1684; the Truce of Ratisbon (15 August 1684) guaranteed the new borders for twenty years.
wars.note: Covered on the Nine Years' War page, not on a page of its own that was opened.

wars.name: Nine Years' War

zones.text: Philippsburg besieged 27 September 1688, Mannheim 11 November 1688, the Palatinate laid waste
Staffarda 18 August 1690 to the Treaty of Turin 29 August 1696
Palamos 10 June 1694, Gerona 29 June 1694, Barcelona captured 10 August 1697

wars.outcome: At Ryswick (20 September 1697) France returned Luxembourg and Kortrijk to Spain, Freiburg, Breisach and Kehl to the Empire and Lorraine to Duke Leopold, and 'French control over the entirety of Alsace was officially recognized'; the Treaty of Turin (29 August 1696) had already ended the Savoy front.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession

zones.text: Savoy occupied 1703-1713; Piedmont until Turin was relieved in September 1706; Nice 1707-1713 ('by May 1706, the French held most of Savoy except Turin')
Lille captured by the Allies 22 October 1708 and held by the Dutch until 1713; Tournai 1709
Landau, Kehl and Breisach contested 1702-1714
Landau taken by the Empire 1702, retaken 1703; Kehl and Breisach captured 1703; Landau and Freiburg captured November 1713; Freiburg, Breisach and Kehl returned at Rastatt (7 March 1714)

wars.outcome: Utrecht (11 April 1713) and Rastatt (7 March 1714): France ceded Ypres, Tournai, Menen, Veurne, Fort Knokke and Warneton to Austria, gained the Principality of Orange and the Ubaye Valley, returned Breisach, Kehl and Freiburg and kept Landau.
wars.note: Infobox war dates March 1701 to 7 September 1714.

wars.name: Seven Years' War

zones.text: 'The French captured Marburg in Hesse' (1760)
French invasion of Hanover, Convention of Klosterzeven 1757; French driven back across the Rhine in the winter of 1757-1758

wars.outcome: Treaty of Paris (10 February 1763): 'France cedes its North American possessions east of the Mississippi River' and Louisiana west of it to Spain; France withdrew from Germany in 1762.
wars.note: Infobox war dates 17 May 1756 to 10 February 1763.

certainty.note: A small royal domain among great fiefs; no treaty or survey draws these frontiers and the Cliopatria shapes of 990-1205 are approximate (domain cores of 15,000-37,000 km2, with Aquitaine drawn in only 1139-1151).

Frontiers are approximate even where a treaty is dated: Normandy 1204, Nimes 1229, Bretigny 1360 and Troyes 1420, Arras 1435/1482, the Italian conquests and the Westphalia gains (Oct 1648) are dated but their lines are not drawn by the pages. The Spanish and Savoy frontiers are soft until 1659.

From the Treaty of the Pyrenees (Nov 1659) the frontiers are fixed by treaties (Nijmegen 1678, Ryswick 1697, Utrecht 1713, Rastatt 1714, Paris 1763). The exceptions are the Rhine and Low Countries frontier during the reunions (1681-1697) and the occupied zones, which are soft.

notes:
SCOPE AND PAGE BUDGET. One Cliopatria row ("Kingdom of France", 990..1791, 96 shapes) carries the whole dossier; 14 pages were opened (the budget for more than 30 shapes), all listed in sources[]. 31 of the 96 shapes are marked ok with the note "unverified: page budget" (990, 1003, 1018, 1139, 1152, 1210, 1241, 1279, 1344, 1395, 1402, 1407, 1459, 1463, 1482, 1487, 1497, 1519, 1547, 1588, 1622, 1629, 1632, 1640, 1662, 1670, 1734, 1741, 1744, 1748, 1780). 22 ledger events are confidence 1: the page is silent and the year and land rest on the Cliopatria shape alone (the Burgundy exit of 1003 and return of 1018, the 1305, 1402 and 1407 additions, the 1640 additions in Alsace, Picardy and Artois, the Aquitaine vassal span 990-1138 and its 1139 return, the 1152 loss, the 1250 Toulouse/Poitou apanages, the 1482 Provence and Franche-Comte/Artois entries, the 1497 exit of Franche-Comte, Artois and Roussillon from the shape, the 1564 exit of the Bourbon block, the 1636/1659 Lorraine occupation, the 1741-1744 German-lands occupation). Pages that would have settled more and were not opened: the French Wars of Religion article for 1562-1589 (the Wars-of-Religion zones the group scope asks for are not drawn beyond Henry IV's 1589-1598 war), the Albigensian Crusade article for the years before the royal campaign of 1226, the War of the Austrian Succession for 1741-1748, the Treaty of Troyes and Treaty of Bretigny articles themselves (dates come from the Hundred Years' War page), and Wikipedia's article on each apanage.

WHAT IS NOT SPLIT OR MERGED. The brief asks whether the 801-year row is successive states: it is one state. The Kingdom of France page treats Capetian, Valois and Bourbon rule as one kingdom with one capital history, and rule 2 makes a dynasty change a rename event, so no split was made. The row's umbrella shapes of 1260-1375 (invalid geometry, repaired upstream) were not used; the leaf row's 96 shapes are reviewed one by one. Cliopatria's "Bourbon Kingdom of France" (slug bourbon-kingdom-of-france, 1815..1847, 8 shapes) shares Wikidata Q207162 with this row, and the Kingdom of France page's infobox carries "restorations" of 1814-1848 inside the same state. It is a separate row and slug owned by another group, and in time it follows the First Republic, the Consulate and the First Empire, so folding it in would put a found event after a dissolve. This dossier therefore ends on 21 September 1792 (the page's date) with the First Republic as successor. If the orchestrator decides the Restoration is the same state, the merge belongs to the dossier of bourbon-kingdom-of-france (a found event naming this slug as predecessor) and not here. Dynasty changes inside the state are rename events (rule 2): Capetian to Valois 1328, Valois to Bourbon 1589, absolute to constitutional monarchy 1791.

HOW THE SHAPE IS READ. The Cliopatria France shape is the royal domain plus the lands the crown held directly, but it also contains lands the pages call separate: Navarre inside the shape 1285-1332 (personal union 1284-1328, removed from the solid shape and drawn as vassal_start/vassal_end, following the Tang example), Brittany from 1492 (the Crown lands page dates the union to 1532; the dossier removes it until a new keyframe of 1532-1538), Bearn from 1595 (the page has Bearn and Lower Navarre incorporated in 1620), Naples through 1506 (the Italian Wars page has the French expelled after Garigliano in December 1503), Catalonia 1642-1652 (the Franco-Spanish War page has the Catalan Courts recognise Louis XIII in 1641 and Spain retake Barcelona in 1652; drawn as a vassal span), and the Duchy of Lorraine from 1700 although Ryswick returned it in 1697 and the page dates the acquisition to 1766. Colonies in the 1791 shape (Haiti 130 cells, India, Senegal, Mauritius) are cut from the metropolitan shape because Cliopatria carries them as rows of their own. England in the 1216-1219 shape is Prince Louis's brief foothold in 1216-1217; it is removed and drawn as a contest zone (1216-1217). A stray cell in central Africa in the 1220 shape is dropped as a geometry artefact.

PAGE DISAGREEMENTS. (1) Champagne: the Crown lands page says the county was reunited with the domain at the 1284 marriage (made official in 1361); the Kingdom of France page says 1316; the dossier follows the Crown lands page and notes the other. (2) Toulouse: the Crown lands page says "the king annexed the County of Toulouse" in 1229, but the same page has the lands pass to Alfonso, Count of Poitou, and revert in 1271; the ledger shows 1229 for the Nimes sénéchaussées only, 1250 as the apanage and 1271 as the reversion. (3) Strasbourg: the Nine Years' War page gives 30 September 1681 in one place and 1685 in another; 1681 is used. (4) Cliopatria draws Toulouse and Poitou inside the shape from 1250, before the reversion, so most of the 1271 gain is a change of tenure and not of colour.

GAPS FOR OTHER DOSSIERS (flagged, not filled). Duchy of Burgundy: no Cliopatria shape for 1018-1384; the crown gives the duchy to Robert in 1034 (Crown lands page) and Cliopatria removes it from this shape only in 1056 (new keyframe 1034-1055 corrects this), so the Burgundy dossier must carry the land for 1034-1384 itself. Navarre: the France shape holds Navarre to 1332 while the page ends the union in 1328; the four years 1329-1332 belong to Navarre, whose own row has a gap there. Duchy of Milan: no shape 1502-1525, so the years the French do not hold Milan (1512-1515 and 1525) leave it nobody's in the data. County of Savoy / House of Savoy: gap 1540-1563 against the French occupation. County of Toulouse (1227-1249) and House of Bourbon (to 1594) rows overlap the France shape; the overlaps are noted on the keyframes (1227, 1241, 1540). Duchy of Lorraine: 55 of its 72 cells sit inside the France shape in 1700. The Lyonnais cells added to the shape (24 in 1188, 4 in 1314, 28 in 1540) are explained by no page opened; a gap-filler should check them against a Lyon / Kingdom of Arles source. 1305: 43 Limousin cells not explained by any page opened.

COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER. Gains and losses of the 11th to 13th centuries name holders the Crown lands page does not give (County of Sens, Gatinais, Moret-sur-Loing, Viscounty of Bourges, Ponthieu, Chartres, Artois), the confidence-1 shape additions name only the land (Limousin 1305; Guyenne, Orleanais and Gascony 1402; Auvergne and Languedoc 1407; Artois, Picardy and Alsace 1640), and the 1741-1758 German operations name no state (German lands, Hesse). They are written as descriptive counterparts so the validator accepts them; each needs a dossier or a slug alias before the counterpart check can pass. "Allies (the page names no state)" stands for the 1708 loss of Lille (War of the Spanish Succession page names the Allies only).

GAZETTEER. These places have no gazetteer entry and were replaced by lon/lat circles or by admin1: Vexin, Sens, Evreux, Issoudun, Perigueux, Cahors, Chartres, Angouleme, Tournai, Ypres, Saluzzo, Valenciennes, Saint-Omer, Marburg, Kehl, Breisach, Landau, Toul, Verdun, Chateau-Landon, Moret-sur-Loing, Bresse, Bugey, Gex (Ain used).
